name: DOHMH and DEP Waterborne Disease Risk Assessment Program Annual Report Data: Percentage of interviewed cryptosporidiosis case-patients reporting selected potential risk exposures before disease onset, by Immune Status
description:
This dataset contains annual data from New York City's Waterborne Disease Risk Assessment Program, a joint effort of the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene and the Department of Environmental Protection. Each row represents a year from 1995 to 2022 and reports the percentage of interviewed cryptosporidiosis case-patients who reported selected potential risk exposures before their illness began. Results are broken out by immune status, comparing persons with HIV/AIDS against immunocompetent persons.

The nine columns include the year plus, for each immune-status group, a point estimate and high and low bounds for each reported exposure. Percentages are stored as text values (for example, "35%"). The dataset has 28 rows, one per year.

The data can be used to track trends over time in cryptosporidiosis risk exposures, compare exposure patterns between immunocompromised and immunocompetent patients, and support public health surveillance and waterborne disease risk assessment. It may also be useful for researchers and health officials
